title: Private PAC learning with polynomial VC and iterated-logarithm sample cost
decision_reason: Explicit scholarly formulation, independently authored 2026 corroboration, complete relevant theorem-scope comparisons, duplicate screening, separated A56 adversarial review and technical validation passed. No matching later resolution was located. The stated finite fixed-accuracy inverse-cubic-slack specialization is explicit.
aliases: Private learning near the VC and log-star Littlestone lower bound

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Every finite nonempty domain X and nonempty class C of total functions X -> {0,1}, with VC dimension v>=1 and Littlestone dimension d. A class-dependent randomized learner outputs one complete binary function h, possibly outside C.
problem_fingerprint.dimension: v is the maximum size of a shattered point set. d is the maximum depth of a complete binary tree with X-labeled internal nodes whose every root-to-leaf binary edge sequence is realized by a concept.
problem_fingerprint.data: For every unknown law D on X and every unknown target c in C, n iid examples (x_i,c(x_i)) with x_i~D; no additional examples, public data, chosen-label queries or known D.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Accuracy alpha=1/16, failure beta=1/16, epsilon=0.1, privacy slack delta_n=1/(100 n^3), for integer n>=1. Output privacy under replacement of one entire labeled record holds for all datasets, including nonrealizable ones.
problem_fingerprint.privacy: For all replacement-neighbor S,S' and all sets E of output hypotheses, Pr[A(S) in E] <= exp(0.1) Pr[A(S') in E] + 1/(100n^3).
problem_fingerprint.observable: m_priv(C) is the least positive sample size for which such a learner exists.
problem_fingerprint.target: Are there universal K>0 and integer q>=1 such that m_priv(C) <= K(1+v+log*_2(max{2,d}))^q for every such finite X,C?
problem_fingerprint.logarithms: log*_2(t) is the number of iterated base-two logarithms needed to reach at most one; max{2,d} avoids endpoint conventions.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: K and q are independent of X,C,v,d. At a chosen n the same learner must work for all D and c. It may depend on X,C,n and has no running-time restriction.
problem_fingerprint.scope: One finite-domain, fixed-accuracy and inverse-cubic-slack formulation of the sourced quantitative private-PAC question. No equivalence with all infinite measurable domains, pure privacy, all privacy curves, or the broader combinatorial-characterization question is asserted.

statement_sources.locator: Section 6, first open question, author-manuscript page 33; Section 3.1 and Definition 12 for the model; Theorem 2 for the small-delta regime.
Section 2, paragraph following Open Question 1, PDF page 3; Section 1 footnotes 1-2, PDF page 1, specify small privacy slack and suppressed parameters.

scope_normalization: The source questions suppress accuracy/privacy dependence. The finite, constant-accuracy version here fixes epsilon and alpha,beta to the ABLM22 lower-bound constants and delta_n to an explicit O(1/(n^2 log n)) regime. NST26 explicitly motivates finite classes. This does not add an unverified optimal dependence on every privacy parameter or claim equivalence with the infinite-domain problem. The n-dependent slack is essential: keeping delta a fixed positive constant would permit a subsampling shortcut.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent research followed by a clearly separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: Suppressed privacy parameters could make a fixed-positive-slack formulation vacuous.
Qualitative learnability, proper/pure privacy, computational separation and density estimation can be mistaken for the quantitative target.
Recent product, smoothness and decision-list theorems require checking possible reductions, not just naming a restricted class.
The finite specialization must not be presented as equivalent to the full infinite-domain or all-parameter question.
issues_resolved: Retained explicit inverse-cubic slack and checked the subsampling loophole and general upper-bound substitution.
Compared the complete relevant models and theorem hypotheses of all eleven sources.
Checked the product lower bound against v and d, the finite-domain smoothness substitution, and the feature-count dependence of decision-list learning.
Stated exact source normalization and limits; repeated duplicate searches and read full nearest entries.
second_review.application_check: The applied claim concerns the amount of sensitive data needed to release a complete classifier. It makes no promise about efficient training, an identifiable target formula or practical privacy certification.
second_review.search_limit: No independent proof certification. Some recent partial results are preprints; source access/version limits are recorded individually.

publication_state: Accepted draft and evidence pushed directly to main; no permanent ID or active catalogue entry. Awaiting the next integration batch.

hypothesis_comparison: Realizable binary PAC learning, approximate privacy, unrestricted computation.
The qualitative characterization and a general upper bound are already established.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The quantitative VC/log-star bound is posed separately. The boosting constant may depend on the class, so boosting does not supply the required universal polynomial.

hypothesis_comparison: General finite Littlestone dimension d; upper bound polynomial in d with logarithmic privacy dependence.
Separate online mistake bounds also retain polynomial d dependence.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Putting delta=1/(100 n^3) into the sample inequality leaves logarithmic n factors absorbable into a polynomial in d. It does not yield a polynomial in v+log-star d.

hypothesis_comparison: VC dimension exactly one and finite Littlestone dimension.
Improper and proper variants retain this dimension restriction.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Iterated-logarithm dependence is proved for this special case; the target is uniform over arbitrary v.

hypothesis_comparison: Finite finest Cartesian decomposition into VC-one factors, each with finite Littlestone dimension.
Countable evaluation quotients and stated privacy restrictions.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The factorwise result retains product structure. No reduction of arbitrary finite concept classes to such products with the requested uniform cost is established.

hypothesis_comparison: Disjoint k-threshold minor of length N with a small-slack privacy curve.
Reported lower bound is of order k log-star N.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: As a scope calculation, the minor gives v>=k and d>=floor(log2 N). Thus this lower bound is at most a constant times v(1+log-star d), compatible with a polynomial in the target sum; it is not a superpolynomial counterexample.

hypothesis_comparison: Distribution/density estimation under total-variation loss.
Constructed family varies ambient dimension and is not a binary target concept class.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: This impossibility does not concern realizable zero-one classification with finite Littlestone dimension.

hypothesis_comparison: Cryptographic security and separation quantify over polynomial-time algorithms.
Theorem 37 relies on Theorem 19's explicit computational restriction despite abbreviated wording.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: An efficiency separation does not rule out the unrestricted-time learners allowed here. The discussion retains the statistical question.

hypothesis_comparison: Known distribution family dominated through a known base law and smoothness modulus rho.
Sample cost retains a covering/modulus dependence.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: All laws on finite X can be included with uniform base law and rho(a)=min(|X|a,1), but that substitution retains domain-size dependence. The theorem therefore does not indirectly supply the requested uniform bound.

hypothesis_comparison: Finite hypothesis class over a b-bit domain.
Generic cost is logarithmic in class cardinality, bounded using b times VC dimension.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The extra description-length parameter cannot be discarded; this polynomial bound is not in v+log-star d alone.

hypothesis_comparison: Pure epsilon privacy and proper learning of point functions.
The output hypothesis class is fixed to the point class in the stated lower bound.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Both restrictions are stronger than the present approximate-private, improper model. The lower bound does not refute this entry.

hypothesis_comparison: PAC theorem uses M=|F| feature functions and a term linear in M, up to logarithmic factors.
Winnow is for margin-separated halfspaces in an online model.
resolution_comparisons.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Encoding an arbitrary class by taking F=C retains dependence on |C|. Neither that substitution nor the margin theorem removes the extra parameters in favor of v+log-star d.

independently_authored_corroboration.reason: The author sets are disjoint. Section 2 expressly proposes the same polynomial VC/log-star upper bound after discussing the existing general upper and lower bounds.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: Finite-domain constant-accuracy inverse-cubic-slack specialization of the suppressed-parameter question; no equivalence with all privacy curves is asserted.

nearest_existing.distinction: A set-and-bitstring compression scheme reconstructs every realizable sample. It need not privatize the released records or classifier.
Average-case noisy-parity recovery with a polynomial-time restriction; no output-privacy condition.
Efficient learning of one Boolean family under uniform inputs; no privacy constraint and a different runtime objective.

normalization_checks: Finite X makes the class, output space and all events finite; v>=1 implies d>=1. Labels 0/1 instead of +/-1 do not change the model.

The learner may depend on the known class but must work for every unknown input law and target. Privacy compares all replacement-neighbor datasets, not just realizable samples. No additional data, queries or runtime promise is included.

The source questions suppress privacy/accuracy dependence. Fixed alpha=beta=1/16 and epsilon=0.1 match the ABLM22 lower-bound constants; delta_n=1/(100 n^3) lies asymptotically within its O(1/(n^2 log n)) regime. The finite fixed-parameter question is deliberately narrower than a uniform theorem over all curves or infinite domains.

A fixed positive delta would permit a different, trivial subsampling bound: release a nonprivate learner on k random selected records from n; coupling gives (0,k/n)-privacy. The n-dependent delta here prevents that shortcut.
For finite C, the generic pure-private finite-class learner ensures that a least positive admissible sample size exists. No monotonicity in n is assumed for the n-dependent privacy definition.

The requested polynomial in a sum is equivalent, up to a change of universal constants/exponent, to a polynomial upper bound in the two nonnegative complexity parameters. Max{2,d} only handles logarithm endpoints.
This is one problem family. Pure privacy, efficient training, fixed v, infinite domains and the separate combinatorial-characterization question do not receive additional counts.
